newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar closes weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar closes weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed weaker at C$1.3802 (US$0.7245) on Monday as profit-taking drove the currency down from an early morning high of C$1.3751 (US$0.7272), traders said. * They said the currency strengthened in morning trade after Statistics Canada reported that Canada's monthly real GDP rose 0.8 percent in April after falling 0.2 percent in March.

"The GDP number is telling us that growth is picking up in the second quarter...so it looks like we're heading for the fourth consecutive quarter of above-potential domestic demand growth," said Rob Palombi, economist with MMS International.
"That should be good news for the currency now that the Bank of Canada has given a clear signal on rates," Palombi added.

The Bank of Canada surprised markets on Thursday when it moved to raise its key bank rate by 25 basis points. The rate hike signalled a clear intention to defend the Canadian dollar, which gained almost one U.S. cent last week.
Analysts said markets would now focus on the United States where the Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday and Wednesday to review monetary policy.

Recent economic data has shown little to suggest that inflationary pressure is growing in the U.S. economy, but Fed officials have said they would raise rates in anticipation of those signs to pre-empt a rise in prices.

Analysts discounted the possibility of a rate hike this week, but said the U.S. employment report due to be released on Thursday would indicate whether inflationary pressures were building in the U.S. economy.
"That will go a long way to determining which direction the (Canadian) dollar goes from here on out," said Doug Porter, economist with Nesbitt Burns.
"If that report is quite strong, then it could reverse the gains made by the (Canada) dollar," Porter added.
Traders said weakness in Canada's bond market also hurt the currency.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.30 to C$114.01 to yield 6.886 percent, while the 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.76 to C$106.62 to yield 6.338 percent.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar closed flat at 82.96 Japanese yen and rose to 1.2632 German marks from Friday's 1.2588 marks.
